limits: Program-driven and muted: not a physical keyboard and mouse test, not a blind playtest.

Busy STOP corners in the soak's maximum traffic (morning rush, every car the town allows, double speed): people wait long at a kerb for a gap in the through street (an old man crossing 10 m wants about 13 s), bunch at the corner, and those arriving queue behind them; a walker re-routing from there starts at the same corner. Cars are no longer held long by it (they edge past, or the walkers make way), but walkers can stand bunched at a corner for a minute and turn back from crossings (13 turn-backs in one final soak). Pedestrian gap acceptance and where people wait at a kerb (StreetLife.CanCross, StreetNet kerb points) were not changed.
Right turns into the 4 m streets cut the corner over the verge (StreetNet turn paths, unchanged): a car waits for anybody standing there inside its sweep, by design.
The cars' corridor ahead still does not count dogs (as before); the body sweep counts a walker's dog only beside the car.
longestWaitForPerson (kept for comparison) counts the red light and the STOP before a walker; the soak now judges longestHeldByPerson (AmbientCar.PersonHeldFor) against 40 s.
The desktop app was not replaced; nothing committed.
